S1.title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.description: Particulate nature of matter, nuclear atom, electron configurations, the mole, and ideal gases.

S2.title: Models of Bonding and Structure
S2.description: Ionic, covalent, and metallic models, intermolecular forces, giant networks, and materials.

S3.title: Classification of Matter
S3.description: Periodic table trends, transition elements, and organic functional groups classification.

R1.title: What Drives Chemical Reactions?
R1.description: Measuring enthalpy changes, energy cycles, fuels, and entropy & spontaneity.

R2.title: How Much, How Fast and How Far?
R2.description: Stoichiometry amounts, rate of chemical change (kinetics), and equilibrium extent.

R3.title: What Are the Mechanisms of Chemical Change?
R3.description: Proton transfer (acids/bases), electron transfer (redox), and electron sharing/pair sharing mechanisms.

S1.1.title: Introduction to the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.1.theme_title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.1.description: Kinetic molecular theory, states of matter, phase changes, heating/cooling curves, mixtures, filtration, distillation, and chromatography.

S1.2.title: The Nuclear Atom
S1.2.theme_title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.2.description: Protons, neutrons, electrons, mass number, atomic number, isotopes, relative atomic mass, and mass spectrometry.

S1.3.title: Electron Configurations
S1.3.theme_title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.3.description: Emission and absorption line spectra, Lyman/Balmer series, orbitals s, p, d, f, Aufbau, Hund, Pauli, and successive ionization energies.

S1.4.title: Counting Particles by Mass: The Mole
S1.4.theme_title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.4.description: Avogadro constant, molar mass, empirical/molecular formulas, combustion analysis, molar concentration, and standard solutions.

S1.5.title: Ideal Gases
S1.5.theme_title: Models of the Particulate Nature of Matter
S1.5.description: Boyle, Charles, Gay-Lussac gas laws, combined gas equation, PV = nRT, and real gas deviations at low T / high P.

S2.1.title: The Ionic Model
S2.1.description: Cations, anions, polyatomic ions, giant ionic lattice, lattice enthalpy, electrical conductivity, and solubility.

S2.2.title: The Covalent Model
S2.2.description: Lewis structures, octet rule, VSEPR geometry, bond polarity, intermolecular forces, resonance, formal charge, and hybridization.

S2.3.title: The Metallic Model
S2.3.description: Delocalized sea of electrons, malleability, ductility, thermal and electrical conductivity, and alloys.

S2.4.title: From Models to Materials
S2.4.description: Bonding triangle, van Arkel-Ketelaar diagram, giant covalent networks (diamond, graphite, graphene, SiO2, fullerenes), and addition polymers.

S3.1.title: The Periodic Table: Classification of Elements
S3.1.description: Periods, groups, s/p/d/f blocks, atomic/ionic radii, ionization energy and electronegativity trends, Group 1/17, Period 3 oxides, and transition elements.

S3.2.title: Functional Groups: Classification of Organic Compounds
S3.2.description: Homologous series, IUPAC nomenclature, structural/stereoisomerism (cis-trans, chiral enantiomers), IR spectroscopy, 1H NMR, and mass spec fragmentation.

R1.1.title: Measuring Enthalpy Changes
R1.1.description: Exothermic vs endothermic, enthalpy profile diagrams, activation energy, standard enthalpy of combustion/formation, and calorimetry (q = mcΔT).

R1.2.title: Energy Cycles in Reactions
R1.2.description: Hess's law, enthalpy cycles, bond enthalpies, Born-Haber cycles, lattice enthalpy, enthalpy of hydration and solution.

R1.3.title: Energy from Fuels
R1.3.description: Complete/incomplete combustion, fossil fuels, biofuels, ethanol, hydrogen fuel cells, specific energy and energy density.

R1.4.title: Entropy and Spontaneity
R1.4.description: Standard entropy, ΔS, Gibbs free energy (ΔG = ΔH - TΔS), spontaneity criteria, and ΔG = -RT ln K.

R2.1.title: How Much? The Amount of Chemical Change
R2.1.theme_title: How Much, How Fast and How Far?
R2.1.description: Stoichiometric equations, limiting and excess reactants, theoretical and percentage yield, atom economy, and back titrations.

R2.2.title: How Fast? The Rate of Chemical Change
R2.2.theme_title: How Much, How Fast and How Far?
R2.2.description: Rate of reaction, collision theory, Maxwell-Boltzmann curves, catalysts, rate equations, reaction order, mechanism, and Arrhenius equation.

R2.3.title: How Far? The Extent of Chemical Change
R2.3.theme_title: How Much, How Fast and How Far?
R2.3.description: Dynamic equilibrium, reversible reactions, equilibrium constant Kc, reaction quotient Q, Le Chatelier's principle, and ICE tables.

R3.1.title: Proton Transfer Reactions
R3.1.theme_title: What Are the Mechanisms of Chemical Change?
R3.1.description: Brønsted-Lowry acids/bases, conjugate pairs, pH scale, Kw, titrations, pH curves, Ka, Kb, pKa, pKb, salt hydrolysis, indicators, and buffer solutions.

R3.2.title: Electron Transfer Reactions
R3.2.theme_title: What Are the Mechanisms of Chemical Change?
R3.2.description: Redox, oxidation numbers, oxidizing/reducing agents, half-equations, Winkler method, voltaic cells, electrolytic cells, SHE, Ecell, and electrolysis calculations.

R3.3.title: Electron Sharing Reactions
R3.3.theme_title: What Are the Mechanisms of Chemical Change?
R3.3.description: Homolytic fission, free radicals, photochemical free-radical substitution of alkanes with halogens (initiation, propagation, termination).

R3.4.title: Electron-Pair Sharing Reactions
R3.4.theme_title: What Are the Mechanisms of Chemical Change?
R3.4.description: Heterolytic fission, nucleophilic substitution (SN1/SN2), electrophilic addition to alkenes, Markovnikov's rule, benzene nitration, and carbonyl reductions.
